responses: You can schedule an appointment with your academic advisor through the Navigate app or your college's advising office. First-year students are typically assigned an advisor based on their major or the Exploratory Studies program.
To check your degree requirements and progress, log into PAWS and pull up your Degree Works audit — it shows exactly what's left to complete your degree.
You can declare or change your major through your college's advising office. It's best to talk to an advisor first to understand how it affects your course plan and graduation timeline.

responses: GSU offers free tutoring through the Learning Support Hub and Supplemental Instruction (SI) sessions for historically tough courses like math, chemistry, and economics. You can find schedules on the GSU Tutoring website.
The University Library has extended hours during finals week and offers bookable study rooms through their online reservation system. There's also a Writing Studio if you need help with papers.
If you're struggling in a class, start with your professor's office hours, then check if there's an SI leader assigned to that course — they run free weekly study sessions.
